text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. and nearly 70 other countries agree on landmark pact to open up most of world's US$600 billion telecommunications market, paving way for unprecedented wave of competition in phone service.
- South Korean government puts army troops and police on alert in and around Seoul after top-level defector shot by suspected North Korean agents and left brain dead.
- Reports that Deng Xiaoping, 92, suffered massive stroke last week bolstered by diplomats who said they received similar information from variety of sources.
- Hong Kong set to get own version of Disneyland, with theme park dedicated to territory's energetic movie industry.

- Singapore Airlines sees open skies pact concluded this month between Singapore and U.S. as important first step towards multilateral agreement spelling increased commercial opportunities for airline, deputy chairman Cheong Choong Kong says.
- Singapore Airlines will have available for sale six Airbus A310 jets within the next 12 months.
- Hong Kong-listed Sum Cheong International buys 15 million shares or 2.95 percent of Berjaya Industrial Bhd's share capital for M$45 million.
- Protectionism in Asia's financial sector could impede region's future economic growth unless major reforms to liberalise industry initiated, report warns.
- Thai government accuses money dealers in offshore markets of planting reports of imminent devaluation of baht, leading to heavy selling of Thai stocks.
- Clampdown on illegal workers, new regulations and higher material prices push up construction costs by at least seven percent in last six months.

- Weak yen and its positive impact on corporate profits leading to reassessment of Japanese stock market, with analysts predicting Tokyo's Nikkei-225 stock average will push firmly above 19,000 level this week.

- UPA Corp Bhd, which accounts for about a third of Malaysia's dairy output, expects other business of reconditioning of printing and printing-related machines to contribute half of turnover by next year.
- Hang Seng index in Hong Kong may be set for further rise.

- Cahya Mata Sarawak Bhd applies to Securities Commission and other authorities for flotation of two subsidiaries -- Steel Industry Sarawak Bhd and Sara Premix Bhd -- on second board of Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
